IN THE COURT OF MR. NAVEED AKHTAR LOHAN , CIVIL JUDGE 1 ST CLASS, RAWALPINDI 
 
 
 
 Civil Suit No . 381 8 /2023 
 
 
 
 Ahmed Din 
 versus 
 Zeeshan Ali Khan etc. 
 
 (SUIT FOR DECLARATION, PERMANENT AND MANDATORY INJUNCTION AND RECOVERY OF POSSESSION AND COMPENSATION AS PER CALCUL A TION OF UNIT/SHOP NO- S F-1 8 , AREA OF UNIT 460 SQ.FIT , IN MALL 35, AT PLOT NO. 35/A, POLICE STATION ROAD RAWALPINDI). 
 
 Written Statement on behalf of Defenda nt s No. 0 2 and 06 
 
 The Defen dant s most respectfully submits as under: 
 
 This written statement is being submitted by the M/s Mall 35 a Partnership Firm (hereinafter, the Defendant Firm ). This written statement is being submitted by the Defenda nt Firm through Mr. Syed Hasan Ali Shah who is fully conversant with the facts of the case and has been duly authorized in this behalf. 
 
 Preliminary Objections: 
 
 That the titled suit is bad for misjoinder of parties and is, therefore, liable to be dismissed forthwith. 
 
 Th at a bare perusal of the plaint reveals that the Plaintiff has (i) failed to mention that he has any cause of action against any of the Defendants, (i i ) failed to mention as to how this court has the jurisdiction to entertain the titled suit, (iii) failed to add a paragraph relating to ‘suit valuation’ and court fees, (iv) failed to pay the requisite court fee under the Court Fees Act, 1870 . T he Plaint has been filed in utter disregard of the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 in particular its Orders IV, VI and VII , read with its Appendix A . Thus, the titled suit is not proceedable and is liable to be dismissed /rejected forthwith with exemplary costs. 
 
 That in addition , it is pertinent to mention that apparently the titled suit is a classic example of frivolous litigation and has been filed by the Plaintiff without any basis merely to avoid his contractual liabilities under the Agreement dated 22-06 -2020 (the ‘ Agreement ’) . Thus, the titled suit is liable to be rejected with exemplary costs. 
 
 Preliminary Submissions: 
 
 That the titled suit is me rely an attempt of the Plaintiff to deceive this learned Court and abuse the process of law by disguising his own failure to fulfill the contractual obligations arising out of the Agreement , whereby the Plaintiff agreed to purchase a Unit No. S F-16 , measuring 460 Square Foot against a total sale consideration of PKR. 13,3 00,000/- ( thirteen million three h un dred t housand only / - (henceforth the ‘ Purchase Price ’). 
 
 That under Clause 3 .3 of the Agreement , the Applicant was under an oblig ation to pay the adjusted price in case of any price escalation . Clause 3 .3 of the Agreement is being reproduced as under: 
 
 “ 3. PAYMENT 
 3.3 The purchase price of the purchased Unit shall remain fixed under this Agreement. However, the Purchase Price may be adjusted if, between the date of singing of this Agreement and the Completion Date, there is an increase in the price of Component Material, as per the price indices published by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics insofar as applicable, or if there is an increase in applicable Taxes or levy of any new Taxes. In this event, the Developer will make every reasonable effort for the Purchase Price to remain unaffected and ensure that any impact on the remaining Purchase Price is adjusted in a fair and reasonable manner (“Adjusted Amount”) . 
 
 The above clause is self - explanatory and clearly shows that the titled suit has been filed by the Plaintiff without any basis , merely to avoid his contractual liabilities under the Agreement. The titled suit is liable to be dismissed with exemplary costs on this score alone . 
 
 On Merit s : 
 
 Corresponding para needs no reply . However, it may kindly be noted that the Mall 35 is not a joint venture of Zameen.com, Zameen Development and Elahi Baksh group. Suit is defective on account on misj oinder of parties , therefore, not proceedable in the present form . 
 
 Contents of the para under reply are d enied being misleading and incorrect . The answering Defendant /Defendant Firm is the sole developer of the Project i.e., Mall 35 (the “ Proje c t ”) and Defenda nt s No. 1, 3, 4 , 5 and 6 ha ve no nexus wit h the ownership of the property. Due to hike in prices of the component construction materials, the Defendant Firm was compelled to escalate the prices as provided in Clause 3 of the Agreement. The Defendant Firm rightly served the demand notice dated 02 -01-2023 demanding Rs. 3,193,206 /- on account of the adjusted amount as per the terms of the Agreement . The demand notice was served upon the Plaintiff by the Defendant Firm only. The Plaintiff has tried to mislead this Hon’ble Court while alleging that the notice was served by the Defendant No.1, 3 and 5. 
 
 Corresponding para is denied being incorrect . The answering Defendant/Defendant Firm has already issued a News-Letter for change of completion date of project. 
 
 The contents of the corresponding para are vehemently denied being concocted and incorrect. 
 
 Contents of para 5 to 7 are denied being misleading and devoid of merits . 
 
 Contents of para 8 are not denied to the ext e nt of issuance of price escalation notice by Defendant No. 2 as per the Agreement . R est of the paragraph is denied being misleading and irrelevant . 
 
 Contents of para No. 9 are vehemently denied being misleading and self-contradictory . No notice was served upon the Plaintiff by EBCO and/or Zameen Developments as alleged by the Plaintiff. The Plaintiff has deliberately distorted the facts to mislead this hon’ble court. 
 
 Contents of para No. 10 are denied being irrelevant and misleading. However, the Defendant Firm rightly issued the Price Escalation Notice . 
 
 The contents of Para No. 1 1 are conco c ted and misconceived, hence vehemently denied . 
 
 Contents of Para No.12 are denied being concocted. The Plaintiff is put to strict proof of his averments regarding loss of reputation and mental anguish. 
 
 Wherefore, it is most respectfully prayed that the suit under reply may kindly be dismissed with cost. 
 
 
 
 Defendant No. 2 and 6
